sentences.text: Brontosaurus was a large, quadrupedal dinosaur characterized by a long neck and a tail that ended in a whip-like structure.
Its forelimbs were shorter than its hindlimbs, giving the animal a distinctive stance.
Although the skull has never been found, scientists believe it was similar to that of the closely related Apatosaurus.
A distinct depression on the back of the shoulder blade helps distinguish Brontosaurus from Apatosaurus, which lacks this feature.
The largest known specimens of B. excelsus could reach a length of 22 meters and weigh up to 15 tonnes.
Computer simulations suggest the long, tapering tail resembled a bullwhip capable of producing a cracking sound over 200 decibels, comparable to a cannon.
A 1925 silent film famously depicted a Brontosaurus fighting an Allosaurus using special effects created by Willis O'Brien.
The assembly of a Brontosaurus skeleton served as a major plot point in the 1938 film Bringing Up Baby.
The U.S. Postal Service issued Brontosaurus stamps in 1989, sparking controversy over the use of the name instead of the scientific Apatosaurus.
The genus Brontosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879.
The type species Brontosaurus excelsus was named based on a partial skeleton without a skull discovered in Como Bluff, Wyoming, by William Harlow Reed.
Several authors later transferred the species to the genus Apatosaurus following its initial description.
Recent evidence suggests Brontosaurus was a fully terrestrial animal, contradicting older theories that it lived partly submerged in water.
Historically, it was thought that sauropods like Brontosaurus were too large to support their own weight on land and likely lived partially submerged in water or swamps.
Research suggests Brontosaurus likely possessed an avian-style respiratory system to help regulate body heat.
Trackways indicate Brontosaurus could travel an average of 20 to 40 km per day and reach speeds of 20 to 30 km/h.
The single forelimb claw was likely used for grasping tree trunks while rearing up to feed, rather than for defense or foraging.
An alternative method estimated Brontosaurus grew 520 kg per year and reached full mass before about 70 years old.
The number of sacral vertebrae, increasing to five at maturity, was one of the first identified growth factors for Apatosaurus.
Peterson and Gilmore theorized that sauropods never stopped growing to attain massive size, a concept unsupported by fossil evidence.
The robust cervical vertebrae of Brontosaurus had expensive energy requirements, suggesting their evolution served an important function.
Diplodocids like Brontosaurus are frequently depicted holding their necks in an upright position to eat from tall trees.
A 2015 study by Emmanuel Tschopp and colleagues determined that Brontosaurus is a distinct genus rather than a synonym of Apatosaurus.
Robert T. Bakker argued in the 1990s that Apatosaurus excelsus should remain a separate genus from Apatosaurus ajax.
Brontosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages, approximately 156 to 146 million years ago.
It inhabited the Morrison Formation of present-day Utah and Wyoming.
The family Diplodocidae, to which Brontosaurus belongs, first evolved in the Middle Jurassic in what is now Georgia before spreading across North America in the Late Jurassic.
The taxonomic status of Brontosaurus remains debated, with some paleontologists still arguing it is a synonym of Apatosaurus.
